title: I Heard My Baby Screaming From the Bathroom—Then I Found My Husband’s Stepmother Trying to Shut the Toilet Lid

blocks.text: I knew something was wrong the moment I heard the screaming.
It was the kind of scream that makes a mother’s entire body react before her mind has time to understand what is happening.
I had been upstairs folding tiny clothes when I heard it.
For three weeks, I had learned every sound my son made—the hungry cry, the tired whimper, the little noises he made when he was dreaming.
The downstairs bathroom door was half open.
And both of her hands were gripping the toilet lid.
For half a second, my brain refused to understand what I was looking at.
Then the screaming cut through everything.
I pulled it open so violently that pain shot through my wrist.
His face was bright red from screaming. His little arms were jerking helplessly, and his cries echoed against the bathroom walls.
I pressed him against my chest and backed away from Margaret.
“What were you trying to do to my baby?”
At that moment, my husband, Daniel, came running downstairs.
“I don’t know. I heard him screaming. I came downstairs, and she was trying to close the lid.”
“I swear to you, I found him like that.”
I wanted to believe there had to be another explanation.
An ambulance took my son to the hospital.
Thankfully, after several terrifying hours, the doctors told us he was going to be okay.
But the police investigation changed everything.
And that’s when something strange appeared.
Our downstairs hallway camera had recorded Margaret entering the bathroom.
It was the blanket I had wrapped around my son earlier that afternoon.
Seven minutes later, I came running downstairs.
There was no footage showing anyone else entering the bathroom.
“Where was the baby before you went into the bathroom?”
Daniel stood beside me, completely silent.
Then the officer asked something that made my stomach twist.
“When was the last time you personally saw your son?”
“About twenty minutes before I heard him screaming.”
The officer exchanged a look with his partner.
“I saw her standing outside the nursery.”
“She had your hair. Your clothes. From behind, I thought it was you.”
But then one detective asked to see our baby monitor.
Then, at 2:13 p.m., the screen went black for approximately thirty seconds.
Margaret immediately said, “I don’t know anything about that.”
A second device had connected to the baby monitor that afternoon.
It had been connected through our home’s Wi-Fi.
But the phone itself wasn’t found in the house.
Instead, they discovered something much worse.
The device belonged to a prepaid phone registered two months earlier.
And the purchase location was only a few miles from our home.
The police asked me whether I knew anyone who lived nearby.
A woman who had approached me at the hospital after Ethan was born.
And she had said something I thought was strange at the time.
The detective showed me a photograph from a security camera near the store where the phone had been purchased.
The woman who had been standing outside my nursery.
The police discovered she had been watching our family for weeks.
Then they found the final piece of evidence.
And in the middle was a picture of my newborn.
Underneath the photograph was a handwritten sentence:
But when investigators questioned her, she refused to explain why she had taken my baby.
Instead, she kept repeating the same thing.
“Rebecca claims she is your husband’s biological mother.”
Daniel’s mother had died when he was a child.
The name listed as his mother wasn’t the woman we knew as Margaret.
Margaret had married Daniel’s father years later and raised him.
Why had Rebecca tried to put my baby in the toilet?
The detective explained what they believed happened.
